st.headline: Japan’s Nikkei plummets 3% as oil prices surge
st.teaser: Markets anxious that Middle East tensions and surging oil prices could fuel inflationary pressures.
fullText: TOKYO – Japan’s Nikkei index plummeted more than 3 per cent in early trading on Sept 11, with markets anxious that renewed tensions in the Middle East and surging oil prices could fuel inflationary pressures.
At around 9.15am local time (8.15am Singapore time), the Nikkei 225 was down 3.03 per cent at 63,291 points.
The international benchmark Brent crude was still up 0.5 per cent at US$108.15 after surging 6.34 per cent the previous day.
The benchmark US oil contract, West Texas Intermediate, jumped above US$100 a barrel on Sept 10 after Yemen’s Houthis seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha .
Major Wall Street indexes spent the entire session in the red, with the S&P 500 falling 0.6 per cent, dropping for a fourth straight day.

“Although President (Donald) Trump has said that the war will end after the November midterm elections , there is no way that the market can believe this claim, as the situation remains perilous,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. AFP

cna.headline: NFL-49ers beat Rams 27-7 in landmark Australia game
cna.teaser: NFL-49ers beat Rams 27-7 in landmark Australia game
fullText: MELBOURNE, Sept 11 : Brock Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns as the San Francisco 49ers opened their season with a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams on Friday in the National Football League's first regular-season game in Australia.

Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, the reigning NFL MVP, had no touchdowns and was pulled late in the fourth quarter as the preseason Super Bowl favourites lost to their division rivals in front of a massive crowd of 100,021 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

The attendance on a local workday - the morning kick-off suiting a U.S. prime-time audience - was the seventh largest for a regular-season NFL game, and second only to the 49ers-Cardinals match-up at Mexico City's Azteca in 2005 (103,467) among international games.

"What an atmosphere to get a win in," said 49ers tight end George Kittle. "The boys played well. The juice was there all day, and I mean, anytime you get a win versus division opponent is always a great thing.
The 49ers had landed in Melbourne a week before the game to overcome jet lag and adjust for the time-zone difference with the U.S. West Coast.
And their players were cheered warmly as they ran out onto the sprawling, oval-shaped playing field having endeared themselves to locals with their high praise for Melbourne's coffee and food scene.

There were loud boos for the Rams, though, who arrived only the day before the game and stuck to their normal U.S. routines, and that strategy may come under the microscope after they were dominated for much of the game.

49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro scored the first points with a field goal with 6:15 remaining in the first quarter but the Rams hit back in the second when Stafford found receiver Puka Nacua with a 41-yard pass to set up a 5-yard touchdown run from Kyren Williams.

Both teams were moving the ball well on the ground but interceptions prevented any further scores until Demarcus Robinson caught a 39-yard pass from Purdy to put the 49ers 10-7 up with 4:28 left in the half.
With Stafford struggling to get his passing game going under pressure from the 49ers' defensive line, San Francisco ramped up the intensity early in the third.
Wide receiver Mike Evans celebrated his first touchdown for his new team when he connected with Purdy on a 2-yard pass as the 49ers went ahead 17-7.
The San Francisco defense then denied Nacua and Stafford, on a quarterback sneak, touchdowns by inches on consecutive plays late in the quarter.
Purdy took the 49ers straight up the other end for another touchdown on a 15-yard pass to Deebo Samuel early in the fourth.
There was no way back from there for the Rams, and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan extended his winning record to 12-7 in his coaching rivalry with Sean McVay.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

listening.title: Singapore Expands Active Mobility Infrastructure to Ease Daily Commutes
listening.transcript: As Singapore expands its cycling path network to cover over one thousand kilometers by 2030, residents are increasingly opting for active mobility. The government is actively upgrading infrastructure around residential estates to make commuting more seamless. However, safety concerns persist regarding the integration of personal mobility devices on shared pathways. Authorities are emphasizing public education to foster a culture of mutual respect among pedestrians and riders.

economistArticle.title: Can Germany’s economic recovery outrun the AfD?
paras: After months of stagnation, Germany’s economy is showing tentative signs of life. Industrial orders are ticking upward, inflation is finally cooling, and consumer confidence is starting to shake off its winter chill. Yet, this nascent recovery is incredibly fragile, overshadowed by structural headwinds and persistent energy costs. For Chancellor Olaf Scholz’s fractious coalition government, the stakes could not be higher as they desperately seek a sustained economic turnaround.

The urgency is fueled by the alarming political ascendancy of the Alternative for Germany (AfD). The far-right party has capitalised on widespread economic anxiety, high immigration, and resentment over green transition policies. With key regional elections looming, the AfD’s populist rhetoric is finding fertile ground among voters who feel left behind by globalization. If the economic engine fails to rev up soon, the political landscape of Europe's largest economy could be permanently altered.

Many economists argue that Germany’s current malaise is not merely cyclical but deeply structural. Decades of underinvestment in digital infrastructure and an over-reliance on cheap Russian gas have left the industrial powerhouse vulnerable. While some manufacturers have successfully pivoted to alternative energy sources, others are quietly relocating operations abroad. This creeping deindustrialisation poses a severe threat to the high-paying jobs that have long underpinned Germany's social cohesion.

Furthermore, the government's fiscal hands are tightly bound by the self-imposed 'debt brake,' a constitutional limit on borrowing that restricts public spending. Critics contend that this fiscal orthodoxy is self-defeating, preventing the very investments needed to modernise the economy and appease disgruntled citizens. Without the leeway to fund sweeping social programs or subsidise transition costs, the coalition remains constrained in its ability to counter populist narratives.

Ultimately, a mild cyclical rebound may not suffice to stem the populist tide. Voters require tangible improvements in their living standards and clear assurances that the green transition will not bankrupt them. If the economic recovery remains anaemic and imperceptible to ordinary citizens, the AfD will continue to exploit the vacuum. Germany’s political stability is now inextricably linked to its economic fortunes, and time is running out.
economistArticle.cn:
经历了数月的停滞，德国经济正暴露出微弱的复苏迹象。工业订单有所上升，通胀终于开始降温，消费者信心也开始摆脱冬日的寒意。然而，这种处于萌芽状态的复苏极其脆弱，面临着结构性阻力以及持续高企的能源成本的阴影。对于奥拉夫·朔尔茨总理脆弱的执政联盟而言，随着他们拼命寻求持续的经济好转，这其中的赌注再高不过了。
这种紧迫感因德国选择党（AfD）令人担忧的政治崛起而加剧。这个极右翼政党利用了普遍存在的经济焦虑、高移民率以及对绿色转型政策的怨恨。随着关键的地方选举临近，该党的民粹主义言论在那些感到被全球化抛弃的选民中找到了肥沃的土壤。如果经济引擎不能尽快加速，这个欧洲最大经济体的政治版图可能会被永久改变。
许多经济学家认为，德国目前的困境不仅是周期性的，而且是深层次结构性的。数十年来对数字基础设施的投资不足，以及对廉价俄罗斯天然气的过度依赖，使这个工业强国变得脆弱。虽然一些制造商已成功转向替代能源，但另一些制造商正悄悄将业务迁往海外。这种渐进的去工业化对长期支撑德国社会凝聚力的高薪岗位构成了严重威胁。
此外，政府的财政手段受到自身施加的“债务刹车”的严格限制，这是一项限制公共支出的宪法借贷限制。批评人士认为，这种财政正统观念是自相矛盾的，阻碍了现代化经济和安抚不满公民所需的投资。由于缺乏资金来支持广泛的社会项目或补贴转型成本，联盟在应对民粹主义叙事方面的能力仍然受到制约。
最终，温和的周期性反弹可能不足以阻止民粹主义的浪潮。选民需要生活水平的切实改善，以及绿色转型不会让他们破产的明确保证。如果经济复苏依然无力且普通公民无法察觉，德国选择党将继续利用这一真空。德国的政治稳定现在与其经济命运密不可分，而时间正在一分一秒流逝。

gems.s: The far-right party has capitalised on widespread economic anxiety, high immigration, and resentment over green transition policies.
gems.why: It showcases a clean tripartite structure (three parallel noun phrases) used to explain complex socioeconomic grievances, which is a classic feature of persuasive, analytical writing. 这是一个经典的排比名词短语结构（由三个并列名词短语组成），用于解释复杂的社会经济矛盾，是极具说服力和分析性写作的典范。

gems.s: Germany’s political stability is now inextricably linked to its economic fortunes, and time is running out.
gems.why: This sentence demonstrates the use of a powerful adverb-verb collocation ('inextricably linked') followed by a punchy, independent clause ('and time is running out') to create urgency. 该句展示了强有力的副词与动词搭配（'密不可分'），随后接上一个短促、独立的分句（'时间正在一分一秒流逝'），从而营造出强烈的紧迫感。
